problems.stem: An instructional bar chart compares test scores across three teaching methods. Which alt text best serves a screen-reader user?
options: A colorful bar chart with blue, green, and orange bars on a white background.
Bar chart: scores were highest for inquiry (82), then lecture (74), then lab (70), showing inquiry led by 8 points.
problems.explanation: Alt text conveys the image's instructional function, the comparison and its takeaway, not its appearance or file metadata.

problems.stem: A page has a decorative corner flourish and a labeled circuit diagram that learners must read. How should their alt attributes differ?
options: Both should get the same generic alt text.
The flourish gets empty alt so screen readers skip it; the circuit diagram gets alt that carries its components and connections.
The flourish needs a long description; the circuit diagram can be left with empty alt.
problems.explanation: Classify first. Decorative images take empty alt to avoid noise; meaningful images need alt that conveys their content. Reversing this is a common error.

problems.stem: An AI tool generates a status legend that marks safe steps green and risky steps red, with no other label. Before shipping, what accessibility judgment must you apply?
options: Accept it, since red and green are intuitive.
Recognize that color-only coding excludes color-blind learners; add text labels or patterns so the safe-versus-risky distinction survives without color.
Make the red brighter so it stands out more.
problems.explanation: Meaning must not be carried by color alone. Adding labels or patterns keeps the distinction usable in color blindness and grayscale, which the tool will not enforce for you.

problems.stem: A multi-series line graph with twelve data points per series is too rich to capture in a short alt attribute. What is the best accessible solution?
options: Write a single 250-word alt attribute containing every value.
Give a brief alt naming the graph's purpose and trend, plus a nearby data table or long description holding the full values.
Leave the alt empty, since the graph is complex.
Replace the graph with the word graph.
problems.explanation: Alt text should stay brief. Complex visuals pair a short alt with a longer description or data table the learner can read in full, rather than overloading the alt attribute.
